# `m.indices.daily_open_close`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

One day's opening, closing, high, and low levels of each index.

```python
m.indices.daily_open_close(symbols, date)
```

| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol` |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Daily Ticker Summary (OHLC) (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Indices Basic | End-of-day, All history |
| Indices Starter | 15-minute delayed, All history |
| Indices Advanced | Real-time, All history |
| Indices Business | Real-time, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `symbol`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under." | REST |
| `Date` | String | The day the summary covers, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: a New York calendar day. From REST `from`: "The requested date." | REST |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the day the summary covers, as an Instant: 00:00 New York time of `Date`. | REST |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the day the summary covers, as an Instant: 00:00 New York time of the next day. For indices that end is an hour later, 01:00 New York time, since whether an index day bar covers the New York or the Chicago day is not verified. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `Open` | double | The open value for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `High` | double | The highest value for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `Low` | double | The lowest value for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `Close` | double | The close value for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `AfterHours` | double | The close value of the ticker symbol in after hours trading. | REST |
| `PreMarket` | double | The open value of the ticker symbol in pre-market trading. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
